title: Pilot ladder rigging rules: climb height, securing, checks and replacement
thumbnailText: RIG IT LIKE YOU CLIMB IT

scenes.label: PILOT TRANSFER
scenes.heading: Rig it wrong, and the pilot can fall.
scenes.narration: A pilot ladder is life-saving equipment. Rig it wrong, and the person climbing it can fall.

scenes.label: HEIGHT OF CLIMB
scenes.heading: Pilot ladder alone: 1.5 to 9 m
scenes.narration: Alone, a pilot ladder covers a climb of 1.5 to 9 metres. Above 9 metres, add an accommodation ladder.

scenes.label: WHERE IT HANGS
scenes.heading: Clear, inside the parallel body, flat on the hull
scenes.narration: Hang it clear of discharges, inside the parallel body, every step flat against the hull. The pilot sets the height of the lowest step.

scenes.label: SECURING
scenes.heading: Strong points, not shortcuts
scenes.narration: Secure it to strong points rated at least 48 kilonewtons, never to the accommodation ladder platform.

scenes.label: AT THE ACCESS POINT
scenes.heading: Ready before the pilot boat arrives
scenes.narration: At the access point: a lifebuoy with self-igniting light, a heaving line, two manropes, and a responsible officer talking to the bridge.

scenes.label: FROM 1 JANUARY 2028
scenes.heading: Ladder withdrawn from service after
scenes.narration: From 2028, a ladder leaves service after 30 months in use, or 36 months from manufacture, whichever comes first.

scenes.label: KEY TAKEAWAY
scenes.heading: Inspect before and after every use
scenes.narration: Inspect it before and after every use. Rig it as if you were climbing.

factCheck.notes: Checked against MSC.576(110): climb 1.5-9 m and combination above 9 m (3.2); clear of discharges, parallel body, steps firmly against ship's side, lowest step as pilot requests (12); strong points/shackles breaking strength not less than 48 kN (6.1); never secured to accommodation ladder lower platform (13.1.6); lifebuoy with self-igniting light, heaving line, two manropes (15.1); responsible officer with communication to bridge (3.7); inspection before and after each use (25.1); withdrawal at 30 months in service or 36 months from manufacture (30). 1 January 2028 application of stowage/maintenance/inspection/operation parts confirmed by DNV (amended SOLAS V/23, MSC.572(110)).

meta.description: How to rig a pilot ladder the way the new IMO pilot transfer standards require: 1.5 to 9 metres climb, position clear of discharges and flat on the hull, 48 kN strong points and the gear at the access point. From 1 January 2028 ladders also leave service after 30 months in use or 36 months from manufacture.
